messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: cont-batching path p99 latency > SLO (us-west-2) - detected 3891234566
incident-bot: symptom: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 spiking to 2.1s for streaming endpoints; error rate normal; customer impact: increased response latency for streaming and batched endpoints
jun (oncall): on it. looking at dashboards now, thanks
amira: seeing correlated surge in mixed-seqlen jobs from api-key: prod-frontend-23, heavy short+long combo
samir: interesting — cont-batcher log shows lots of large-batch assemble waits while streaming workers starve. tail latency for small sequences amplified when they join large batches
jun (oncall): can we route streaming traffic away from cont-batching nodes temporarily? what's safe toggle?
kev: we have a runtime flag: --prefer-stream-only and scheduler-level annotation batcher.mode=prefer_stream. ops-runner can flip via k8s patch on deploy config
ops-runner: can do immediate patch to deployment/redwood-batcher-usw2 to set env BATCHER_MODE=stream_prefer. Doing dry-run first
jun (oncall): also want to reduce max_batch_size preemptively for cont-batcher to limit amplification. current max_batch_size=128, suggest 64 for 10m window
amira: agree. 64 will reduce KV cache pressure and shorten assemble delays. Might increase overall token cost slightly but reduce p99
ops-runner: patch applied: 
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-batcher-usw2 BATCHER_MODE=stream_prefer
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-batcher-usw2 MAX_BATCH_SIZE=64
```
ops-runner: changes rolled to 3/3 pods (rolling restart)
jun (oncall): monitoring traces...
samir: grabbing logs from one host: cont-batcher.log shows repeated "waiting_for_batch: 350ms" and then one huge assemble -> execution time that blocks streamer threads
kev: can we enable preemptive packing? there is a knob PREEMPT_THRESHOLD_MS = 200
jun (oncall): enable for a short window. ops-runner please set PREEMPT_THRESHOLD_MS=200 and BATCH_ASSEMBLE_TIMEOUT_MS=250
ops-runner: applying env changes now
ops-runner: applied PREEMPT_THRESHOLD_MS=200 BATCH_ASSEMBLE_TIMEOUT_MS=250 to redwood-batcher-usw2, rolling restarts continuing
amira: quick note: watch for throughput drop on high-seqlen workload if we preempt too aggressively
samir: started a small synthetic load mimicking short+long mix, p99 immediately dropped from ~2.1s -> 420ms on test nodes
jun (oncall): production dashboards show p99 trending down to 480ms, p95 ~ 180ms. still above ideal but much improved
kev: open question: eviction of KV cache entries when mixed lengths hurt long-lived sessions. consider targeted KV eviction for very-long sequences to free compute slots
amira: can we temporarily increase streaming-only capacity instead? spin up additional stream-only pool to absorb short-sequence traffic
ops-runner: launching 2 additional stream-replica pods (stream-only config) in usw2:replica-set-stream-only. ETA ~ 90s
support-bot: received 3 customer tickets referencing slow responses; flagging priority customers with affected api-keys: prod-frontend-23, partner-invoice-7
jun (oncall): pushing incident update to #incidents and status page: "We are investigating elevated latency affecting some streaming calls in us-west-2. Mitigations in progress."
samir: logs show one noisy job from api-key prod-frontend-23 with huge seq len 27k tokens started at 3891234500. That likely triggered batch amplification. Recommend rate-limiting that key temporarily
jun (oncall): @support-bot can you reach out to account team for prod-frontend-23 and ask to throttle or move heavy job to dedicated capacity while we stabilize?
support-bot: pinged account team, attaching support ticket id: #17289. Customer notified about temporary mitigation suggestion
ops-runner: stream-only pods are up; routing rules update applied: ingress-routes now prefer stream-only pool for requests with header x-priority=short-seq (we infer lengths). Rolling steering happening
jun (oncall): p99 now ~320ms, p95 150ms. error rates still normal. feeling like incident largely mitigated but keep monitoring for 30m
amira: agree. we'll keep PREEMPT_THRESHOLD and reduced MAX_BATCH_SIZE for 20m then slowly revert if stable
kev: make sure to record this as a handoff note — cause: mixed sequence length amplification in continuous batching path + oversized max_batch_size + delayed preemption. Mitigations: reduce max_batch_size, enable preemptive threshold, route short sequences to stream-only pool, notify customer to throttle heavy long job
jun (oncall): preparing handoff to night oncall in 15m. leaving runbook steps and commands in thread. will include timestamps and links to dashboard snapshots
jun (oncall): handoff notes:
- trigger: p99 spike 2.1s detected 3891234566
- root cause hypothesis: cont-batcher assembling large batches with heterogeneous seq lengths -> long assemble/execution holds streaming threads -> tail amplification
- mitigations applied: set MAX_BATCH_SIZE=64, BATCHER_MODE=stream_prefer, PREEMPT_THRESHOLD_MS=200, BATCH_ASSEMBLE_TIMEOUT_MS=250; provisioned 2 extra stream-only pods; requested customer throttle
- metrics to watch: p99/p95 for streaming endpoints, queue waiting time distribution, batch size distribution, KV cache eviction rate
- rollback plan: revert MAX_BATCH_SIZE and PREEMPT_THRESHOLD only after 30m of stable p99 < 500ms; revert via same kubectl env set commands
jun (oncall): handing off to samir at 3891234620 — please monitor for 2h and escalate if p99 climbs above 800ms
samir: ack. will monitor and follow escalation procedure. saving logs and grep patterns used. thanks
incident-bot: incident annotated: severity=sev2, owner=jun, started=3891234566, mitigated=3891234620, affected_region=us-west-2
jun (oncall): closing active page. will update postmortem skeleton after 4h if trends stable. :thumbsup:
